precepts.text: Honour thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be prolonged. The Lord knew from the beginning that the inner structure of the home is what builds the nation. When there is dysfunction in the home, it affects the whole nation: households affect other households, your kids learn behaviors from their kids, a gossiping best friend infects your wife, and murmuring company infects you. You will infect the nation if your household is not in order.
precepts.point: Video played in class: a woman will not treat you how she treats her father; she will treat you how her mother treated her father. A child that comes from a household in order is more likely to keep that order; everybody still makes a choice, but the probability follows the household.

note.label: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.why:
Moses repeats the commandment: “Honour thy father and thy mother, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee; that thy days may be prolonged, and that it may go well with thee, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.”

It was so important for them to honour their father and mother so that their days would be prolonged, so they would not die, and so it would go well with them in the land. The Lord knew from the beginning that the inner structure of the home is what builds the nation.

When there is dysfunction, anything not aligned with how God set it up, there are going to be problems, and it affects the whole nation. Certain households affect other households. If your house is out of order and you are best friends with so-and-so, your kids play together and learn the same bad behaviours. If a sister is a gossiper running from home to home and she is your wife's best friend, it is only a matter of time before your wife is called a gossiper too. Same with you: kick it with the murmurers and you will murmur.

You will infect the nation if your household is not in order. God is about order, always has been. A child raised in a household where the father and mother both understood the laws of God, operated within their roles and demanded obedience to God is more likely to carry that legacy on. Everybody still makes a choice, but the probability follows the household.

precepts.text: The secrets of wisdom are double to that which is; the scriptures are twofold, speaking to Egypt then and to spiritual Egypt now.
precepts.point: The Most High is a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate him, and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love him and keep his commandments.
precepts.why:
“And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The scriptures are twofold.

The ten commandments are reiterated here and Israel reminded, because the graven images they knew came from Egypt. But the commandment still pertains today, to spiritual Egypt: against the false images of Christ, the virgin mary statues, the cobblestone at Mecca, buddha and the gods of the east. “Thou shalt not make thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath” spoke to Egypt then and speaks to spiritual Egypt now.

He is a jealous God, “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me, And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me and keep my commandments.” The secrets of wisdom are double, and both sides of the word stand.

precepts.text: Remove far from me vanity and lies; give me neither poverty nor riches; lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord? or lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.
precepts.point: Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain” is not about saying oh my god. Solomon shows how the name is taken in vain: “lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.” Breaking the commandments, stealing, lying, bearing false witness, committing adultery, is how the name is taken in vain.

Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: “Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me: Lest I be full, and deny thee, and say, Who is the Lord?” Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.

precepts.text: The chief things for life are simple; better a poor man's own mean cottage than delicate fare as a freeloader in another man's house.
precepts.point: Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.
precepts.why:
“The chief thing for life is water, and bread, and clothing, and an house to cover shame. Better is the life of a poor man in a mean cottage, than delicate fare in another man’s house.”

The chief things for life are simple, and better a poor man's own mean cottage than delicate fare as a freeloader in another man's house. That is Solomon's spirit in Proverbs 30: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and poverty drives a man to steal and take the name of his God in vain. Keep life simple and the name is not profaned.

precepts.text: His name is called The Word of God; the name of the Most High is his word.
precepts.point: Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.
precepts.why:
“And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God.” The name of the Most High is his word.

That is what it means to take his name in vain. His name is called The Word of God, and the word of God is the book of the commandments; so to profane the commandments, stealing, lying, bearing false witness, committing adultery, is to profane the name. It was never about saying oh my god.

precepts.text: The word of God is the book of the commandments of God, the law that endureth for ever; the name, the word, and the law go hand in hand.
precepts.point: Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.
precepts.why:
“This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” The word of God is the book of the commandments of God, the law that endureth for ever.

His name is called The Word of God, and the word is the book of the commandments: the name, the word and the law go hand in hand. So to take the name of the Lord thy God in vain is to break the commandments, as Solomon shows, “lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain.” They that keep the law shall come to life, and such as leave it shall die, for “the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.”

precepts.text: Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord; walking in the way of God is keeping his commandments.
precepts.point: Ye shall walk in all the ways which the Lord your God hath commanded you, turning aside neither to the right hand nor to the left, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days.
precepts.why:
“Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord.” Walking in the way of God is keeping his commandments.

That is what Moses was given to teach: “Ye shall walk in all the ways which the Lord your God hath commanded you, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days”, turning aside neither to the right hand nor to the left. The undefiled in the way are the ones who walk in the law, and that is the blessing.

precepts.text: I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; Egypt means bondage and slavery.
precepts.point: There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
Here is the nail in the coffin: “And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. What is Egypt? The scripture defines it right in Deuteronomy 5: “I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.” Egypt means bondage, slavery.

So the Most High is saying: I will bring you into slavery again, with ships. He brought us out of the house of bondage once; for not hearkening to his voice he brings us into bondage again, and this time by ship.

precepts.text: I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me, showing mercy unto thousands of them that love me.
precepts.point: This is the visiting of iniquity in the regeneration; after death comes the judgment, when you reform your mind and subdue your own understanding, and you will be kept alive and obtain mercy.

note.label: Psalm 89: The Covenant Made with David

precepts.why:
“If his children forsake my law, and walk not in my judgments; If they break my statutes, and keep not my commandments; Then will I visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with stripes.” The visiting of iniquity is from the law: “for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”.

The same law goes on to the other side, showing mercy unto thousands of them that love him. That is what Psalm 89 says too: “Nevertheless my lovingkindness will I not utterly take from him, nor suffer my faithfulness to fail.” People say mercy is not in the Old Testament, but it is in there, right beside the rod and the stripes.

So the children of David are visited for their transgression, but the covenant is not broken. The jealous God who visits iniquity is the same God whose lovingkindness is not utterly taken away.

points: Hear, O Israel, the statutes and judgments which I speak in your ears this day, that ye may learn them, and keep, and do them. Doing them is the key thing: it is not verbal, actions carry the weight, and the actions are the commandments.
The Lord made not this covenant with our fathers, but with us, even us, who are all of us here alive this day.
The Lord talked with you face to face in the mount out of the midst of the fire, and Moses stood between the Lord and the people to shew the word: Moses was the mediator for Israel.

I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage: Egypt means slavery. This is a good scripture for the brothers who go out to prophesy, because the whole exodus claim can be shown from Deuteronomy 5 without ever leaving the book.

Thou shalt have none other gods before me, and thou shalt not make thee any graven image: the ten commandments are being reiterated and Israel reminded, because the graven images they knew came from Egypt.

The Most High is a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate him, and shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love him and keep his commandments.

Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: this is not about saying oh my god. Solomon shows how the name is taken in vain: lest I be poor, and steal, and take the name of my God in vain. Breaking the commandments, stealing, lying, bearing false witness, committing adultery, is how the name is taken in vain.
His name is called The Word of God, and the word of God is the book of the commandments; so to profane the commandments is to profane the name.

Solomon's prayer is the humble spirit: give me neither poverty nor riches, feed me with food convenient for me. Full riches make a man deny the Most High and forget the congregation and the work, and money has pulled people out of this walk; poverty drives a man to steal. The chief things for life are simple, water, bread, clothing, and an house to cover shame, and the Most High blessed Solomon with riches because riches were not his god.

Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it: six days shalt thou labour, but the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God, and no work is done by thee, thy children, thy servants, thy cattle, nor the stranger within thy gates, that all may rest.
And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the Lord thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand; therefore the sabbath was commanded.

Honour thy father and thy mother, that thy days may be prolonged; thou shalt not kill; neither shalt thou commit adultery; neither shalt thou steal; neither shalt thou bear false witness against thy neighbour, meaning lie.
Neither shalt thou covet: the word used today is jealousy. Being mad that a brother or sister drives better or earns better, keeping up with the Joneses, is an evil spirit that has to be purged.

These words the Lord spake unto all the assembly out of the midst of the fire, of the cloud, and of the thick darkness, with a great voice, and he added no more; and he wrote them in two tables of stone.

The people heard the voice out of the darkness while the mountain burned, and the heads of the tribes came near and said, we have seen this day that God doth talk with man, and he liveth; but why should we die? for this great fire will consume us.
So they asked Moses to go near, hear all that the Lord our God shall say, and speak it unto them: and we will hear it, and do it.
They have well said all that they have spoken: Israel always talked a good game.

O that there were such an heart in them, that they would fear me, and keep all my commandments always, that it might be well with them and with their children for ever. When it came to actions the people did not fear the judgments and the repercussions of breaking the commandments.
Go say to them, get you into your tents again; but as for thee, stand thou here by me, and I will speak unto thee all the commandments which thou shalt teach them.

Ye shall walk in all the ways which the Lord your God hath commanded you, turning aside neither to the right hand nor to the left, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days.
